focus: godot-waikthrough turns a Godot game into a narrated walkthrough film by playing it, capturing the real viewport, and invoking riff to explain mechanism and trade-off

dropped_beats.reason: Anatomy beat explaining the two-mode file structure belongs in the 16:9 long; the Short establishes what the skill does without needing a folder tree
Phase 1 inventory detail (GDD vs built/planned/broken cards) is worked-example depth for the long film; the pipeline overview in B02 covers the concept
Phase 2 capture terminal walkthrough is implementation detail belonging in the long film; B02 establishes that the real viewport is captured
Walker mode four-bookend sequence is advanced-use anatomy; the Short does not need to explain the full bookend ordering to be coherent
Falsifiability/self-demo beat partially overlaps B08 (the honesty contract); the essential limitation — requires a real running game — is preserved in B10 Verdict narration

cut_first_review: B00 introduces Liam and the misconception. B01 corrects it: riffs, not records. B02 gives the five-phase pipeline overview so the viewer understands the shape. B06 zooms in on the riff mechanic (heart of the skill). B08 states the honesty contract — do not secretly fix the game. B10 renders the verdict and names the structural limitation. B11 hands off a paste-ready prompt for the viewer's own Godot project and signs off 'Liam, in for Bear.' B12 is the silent outro. No dangling references: B02→B06 is a natural zoom from pipeline overview to the key step; B08→B10 flows from constraint to verdict; B10→B11 flows from summary to action. The self-demo limitation ('a full build needs a real running game') is present in B10 without needing B09's meta-commentary about the reel itself.
